newsitem.title: USA: Bio-Technology General reports higher sales.
newsitem.headline: Bio-Technology General reports higher sales.

text.p: Bio-Technology General Corp said Monday its sales in the first half of 1997 had increased 50 percent over sales in the second half of 1996.

"We are highly pleased by the 50 percent growth in product sales that we have achieved in the first half of 1997 compared to the first six months of 1996," said Chief Executive Sim Fass. "This increase is accompanied by only a modest increase in expenses of 15 percent over the same time period, allowing for the delivery of substantive growth in earnings per share.
"We are continuing to work towards advancing our product pipeline and maintaining our solidly established position within the biopharmaceutical industry."

Net income for the second quarter of 1997, after income taxes of $1.5 million, was $3.9 million, or $0.08 per share, on revenues of $15.7 million, compared to net income of $2.8 million, or $0.06 per share, on revenues of $12.2 million, in the comparable quarter of 1996.

Product sales for the quarter and six months ended June 30, 1997 increased 26 percent and 50 percent to $14.6 million and $29.0 million, compared to $11.6 million and $19.3 million, respectively, in the comparable 1996 periods.
Expenses for the quarter and six months were $10.2 million and $20.4 million, compared to $9.4 million and $17.8 million, respectively, in 1996.
The company said the increase in expenses was due primarily to increased marketing and sales expenses and an increase in research and development expenses, including clinical studies.
Bio-Technology General Corp develops, manufactures and markets genetically engineered and other products for human health care.
